title: Blush Butterfly Hanging Ornament
subtitle: A two-colour crochet butterfly on a beaded cord with a striped tassel
finished_size: ≈ 18 cm (7 in) plus an 8 cm loop
description: Four teardrop wings worked as stitch fans in a magic ring and edged in cream, joined with a wrapped body and knotted antennae, and hung on a beaded cord above a cream-and-pink tassel.
glance: ≈ 18 cm (7 in) plus an 8 cm loop
size_guide: One size. For a larger ornament use light worsted (#4) cotton and a 3 mm hook; for a smaller one use sport-weight cotton and a 2 mm hook. Beads and tassel length can be changed freely.
gauge: 22 sc and 24 rows/rnds = 10 cm (4 in) in single crochet with a 2.5 mm hook. Gauge is not critical for an ornament, but work firmly so that stuffing does not show and flat pieces keep their shape; sizes depend on your tension.
swatch: Optional density check: ch 12, then work 10 rows of sc on 11 sts. The square should measure about 5 cm (2 in) wide and 4 cm (1.6 in) tall. If it is larger or you see gaps between stitches, use a smaller hook.

materials.item: Yarn A (wing edges, body, tassel, cord)
materials.detail: DK (#3) cotton, cream — approx. 11 m (12 yd), about 5 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, dusty pink — approx. 6 m (6 yd), about 3 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
3 gold-tone beads 6 mm (hole at least 2.5 mm); 2 natural wooden beads 12 mm (hole at least 3 mm). Both cord strands must pass through each bead together — test before you start.
fabric glue (optional), tapestry needle, stiff card, scissors

abbreviations: work the sequence in brackets N times

techniques.name: Magic ring (MR)
techniques.how: Wrap the yarn twice around two fingers, insert the hook under both strands, pull up a loop and ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Work the stitches of Rnd 1 over both strands, then pull the tail firmly to close the centre.

techniques.name: Joining new yarn with a standing sc
techniques.how: Make a slip knot on the hook, insert the hook in the stitch, yo, pull up a loop, yo and draw through both loops. This sc counts as the first stitch.

techniques.name: Tassel neck wrap
techniques.how: Lay a 5 cm loop of the wrapping strand along the tassel, pointing down. Wrap the long end tightly around tassel and loop, from the top down. Pass the end through the loop, then pull the short tail at the top until the loop disappears under the wraps. Trim both ends and hide them in the skirt.

notes: Joined rounds (where a round says "Join"): unless the round says otherwise, start the round with ch 1, which does not count as a stitch, and finish it with a sl st into the first stitch.
Right side: for pieces worked in rounds, the outside of the rounds; for pieces worked in rows, choose the neater side and mark it. "Wrong sides together" means the marked right sides face out.
US crochet terms are used throughout.
The number in parentheses at the end of a row or round is the number of stitches you should have when it is finished. Tick the box when you finish each step.
Rows: ch 1 at the start of a row does not count as a stitch; rounds worked in a magic ring are worked in continuous spirals unless the round says "join".
Leave a 20 cm (8 in) tail when you fasten off a piece that will be sewn; weave in all other ends on the wrong side as you go.

blocks.text: Each wing is a fan of graded stitches worked into a magic ring and pulled into a teardrop, then edged with one round of cream sc.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn B, make a MR, ch 2 (does not count). In the ring work sc 1, hdc 1, dc 2, tr 3, dc 2, hdc 1, sc 1. Pull the ring closed and join with a sl st to the first sc. Fasten off Yarn B.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: Join Yarn A with a standing sc in the first sc; sc 1, (inc, sc 1) x3, inc, sc 2. Join with a sl st to the first sc. Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn B, make a MR, ch 2 (does not count). In the ring work sc 1, hdc 1, dc 4, hdc 1, sc 1. Pull the ring closed and join with a sl st to the first sc. Fasten off Yarn B.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: Join Yarn A with a standing sc in the first sc; (inc, sc 1) x3, sc 1. Join with a sl st to the first sc. Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Lay the wings right side up: the two upper wings with their pointed (ring) ends meeting at the centre and tilted up, the two lower wings below them with their points also at the centre. Sew all four points together with the tails.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Body: fold a 12 cm strand of Yarn A into a 3 cm bundle of 4 strands and lay it vertically over the centre on the front. Wrap a 1 m length of Yarn A tightly round the bundle and the wing centres, from top to bottom, each wrap next to the last, until the wraps cover 2.4 cm (about 12–14 wraps). Sew the end into the back.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Antennae: thread a 15 cm strand of Yarn A under the top wrap of the body so both halves stand up. Tie an overhand knot in each half 1.5 cm from the body and trim 2 mm above the knot. A drop of fabric glue keeps the antennae upright.

blocks.text: The tassel is made first: the hanging cord is tied into its top, so the cord runs through the whole ornament and is anchored in the tassel.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Cut a piece of stiff card 10 cm (3.9 in) tall. Wrap Yarn A around the card 28 times, then Yarn B 12 times spread across the card between the cream wraps (40 wraps). Cut the yarn at the bottom edge.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Cut the hanging cord: one 90 cm (35 in) length of Yarn A. Slide it under all the wraps along the top edge of the card so that its middle sits there, and tie it in a tight square knot around the wraps. Both cord ends now point upwards.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Cut through all the wraps along the bottom edge of the card and remove the card. Let the strands hang down from the cord knot.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.text: Tassel neck: cut a 70 cm length of Yarn B. Measure 2 cm down from the top fold and wrap it tightly 8 times around the bundle (see Tassel neck wrap in Techniques).

steps.label: Step 5
steps.text: Trim the skirt evenly to 9 cm (3.5 in) from the top fold. Hold it over steam (or dampen it) and comb the strands straight with your fingers; let it dry hanging.

items: Thread both cord ends together through a large-eye tapestry needle (or a bead needle with a big eye). Work upwards from the tassel.
String, from the tassel upwards: 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead → the butterfly → 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead.
Butterfly: push the needle up through the body wraps from the bottom to the top, between the antennae.
Push everything down snugly onto the tassel so there are no gaps. Holding both cord ends together, tie one overhand knot right above the top bead to lock the stack.

Hanging loop: tie the two cord ends together with a square knot so that the loop measures 8 cm (3 in) from the overhand knot to the top. Trim the ends to 5 mm and add a drop of fabric glue to the knot if you like.

blocks.label: Safety
blocks.text: This is a decoration, not a toy, and not suitable for children under 3 years. Beads and cords are a choking and strangling hazard: hang it out of reach of babies, young children and pets.

observations.conclusion: Fan of graded sts in a MR + 1 cream sc round

observations.evidence: Wrapped cream body down the centre
observations.conclusion: Yarn wrapped over a small bundle

observations.evidence: Two short antennae with knots/balls at the tips
Cream tassel with pink strands mixed in
Cream cord loop above a gold–wood–gold bead stack; same stack below the piece
observations.conclusion: Cord tied into the tassel top and threaded up through beads and piece

accuracy.text: Sizes are scaled from the photo using the 12 mm wooden beads as the reference; the photos look like rendered images, so stitch counts are a design reconstruction, not a count from a real sample. Make the piece once and compare before selling the pattern.

assumptions: Wing stitch groups are a design reconstruction of the photographed shapes.

closing_note: Thank you for making this ornament. Happy crocheting!
